sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 1.3 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 8) treats only vowel length as a suprasegmental phoneme; footnote 1 on the same page: 'other suprasegmental features occurring in this dialect have not been taken for analysis in this study.' Allophones (1.5), clusters (1.6) and syllabic patterns (1.7, pp. 26-28) contain no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Shyam, S. K. and Pugazhendi, P. and Mini, P.V. (2019). Chetham (Sound), preparation of a Handbook for Kani language of Kannikkar Community. Calicut: Kerala Institute for Research Training & Development studies. 296 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The handbook is in Malayalam; its phonology part inventories 5 short + 5 long vowels (p. 43-44), the diphthong ai (p. 51), 24 consonants with positional distribution (pp. 51-63) and identical/non-identical consonant clusters (pp. 63-66), then goes straight to nouns, gender, number, case, verbs, tense and adverbs. There is no section on syllable structure, stress, accent or prosody; a search of the whole scanned text for stress, accent, prominence, suprasegmental, intonation, pitch, syllable and the Malayalam terms uunnal, svaraaghaatam, balam, aksharaghatana finds nothing. sources.note: Silent. Kani section lists segmental correspondences with Malayalam (a>e, v>m/b, rr>cc, l>y) and a few morphological features; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.note: Kanikkaran appears only in the Dravidian classification list ('UNCLASSIFIED: Allar, Bazigar, Bharia, Kamar, Kanikkaran..'); no accent data for it.

sources.citation: Syam, S. K. 2017. Aspects of Life and Language of Kanikkar Tribal Community of Kerala: A Study. Language in India 17(12) (December 2017): 363-378. ISSN 1930-2940.
sources.note: The 'Phonology of Kani Language' section (pp. 370-371) gives 24 phonemes: 5 vowels /a i e u o/ with phonemic length, 19 consonants plus a marginal alveolar approximant, vowel and consonant charts, then Malayalam a > Kani e correspondence and morphology; there is no statement on tone, pitch, accent or stress anywhere in the article.
